description: Twin-store probes must use the explicit path to OUR binary (/home/denkhaus/dev/mulch/target/debug/mulch), never a bare 'mulch' from PATH: the npm package @os-eco/mulch-cli 0.10.7 installs its own 'mulch' shim on PATH (same name, the reference JS implementation) — a probe round that shells out to 'mulch' compares the reference with itself and silently 'passes'. Caught by the sprint-26 spec reviewer.
resolution: Ad-hoc probe snippets pin the explicit debug path (or CARGO_BIN_EXE_mulch); the battery helpers are already explicit. The trap is the misnamed bare command, not the probe design.

name: parallel-writer-tests-need-unique-dedup-keys
description: Parallel-writer CLI tests (writer-lock class) must give every concurrent writer a UNIQUE dedup key (distinct --name AND --content for conventions — the dedup key is type+content-family). First draft raced 8 records with identical --content: all 8 processes succeeded, but the store held ONE record — correct upsert/dedup semantics, wrong test. The "lost records" assertion then fires for the wrong reason and points at the lock, not the fixture. Same discipline as time-dependent fixtures: assert on a store shape the command cannot legitimately collapse.

Python-written Rust test strings via triple-quoted heredocs corrupt backslash escapes: the file receives double backslashes (the rust string then contains literal backslash-n TEXT and unescaped quotes) -> YAML fixtures become single-line garbage and strings terminate early (E0765). Hit twice in sprint 30 (unit-test drop + debug probe). Rule: write Rust test fixtures with REAL newlines via format!/writeln! or verify the file bytes after any python string insertion; when a yaml-parsing test fails with empty-string fields, check yaml_display-style helpers for a missing String arm first (the sprint-30 yaml_display catch-all collapsed every string to "").
resolution: read back inserted bytes before running; prefer building fixture strings in rust (format!/writeln!); grep helpers for catch-all arms when everything renders empty

name: golden-fixtures-embed-the-capture-instant
description: Reference-byte golden fixtures for time-dependent rendering stay deterministic by embedding the CAPTURE INSTANT: capture the reference output at a noted now, pass that now into our pure fns as a parameter (the fns never read the clock), and the 'Nd ago' ages in the golden match forever. The command layer's trailing console newline belongs to console.log — strip it from goldens or every family pin fails on a phantom difference (sprint 28, four-family render seam).

name: pinned-expectations-share-the-fixture-instant
description: The sprint-18 runtime-clock rule extends to PINNED EXPECTATIONS: when a fixture goes runtime-derived, every assert embedding the volatile value must read the SAME instant the fixture used (return it from the helper) - and twin fixtures must share ONE now (per-process static or a passed-in instant), else ours/theirs stores differ by a now race and read-only assertions fire. Third occurrence (odd_legacy_fixture 2026-10-01 crossed the 14-day shelf on 2026-10-16): both binaries agreed, only the pin flipped.

Twin-store differential probes in Python must mask volatile values on BOTH sides and with BOTH spellings: compact store lines quote recorded_at without spaces but --json pretty output inserts one - a mask regex without optional whitespace silently fails every json comparison; normalizing only OUR side (the echo rename) leaves the reference timestamps raw. Twin git repos commit at different instants: evidence commit shas always differ (mask them); temp-dir paths leak into error bytes. Sprint 31: three probe-harness bugs produced phantom FAILs before the harness was fixed; the binaries had been right.
resolution: mask both sides; regex with optional whitespace; mask commit shas and temp paths; suspect the harness first when both binaries were just rebuilt

name: promote-theirs-battery-direction
description: Promote the REFERENCE side for promote-law byte comparisons; statics promoted, record content never

TIE fixtures share ONE stamp (sprints 36+37 flake, fixed de0e27b): a test pinning ms-granular TIE behavior (e.g. ready's identical-timestamps-keep-config-order) must derive the "identical" recorded_at values from a SINGLE now()-based string, never n separate at()-calls — two consecutive clock reads differ in nanoseconds and straddle a MILLISECOND boundary on roughly 1% of runs, and at ms granularity (both sides' new Date().getTime()) a 1ms difference is NOT a tie: the sort flips to true time order and the test fails only under load. Symptom: passes in isolation, fails ~1 in 100 full-battery runs, reported as 'transient flake' by two different children before the mechanism was found.
resolution: Derive the shared stamp once (let tie = at(N)) and build every fixture line from that one string; a tie test that cannot share stamps should not exist — the tie IS the fixture.

content: Twin-store differential fixtures must seed EACH side with its own binary's shipped strings: our archives carry the promoted restore hint (+3 bytes vs ml). Seeding BOTH twins with the reference banner makes a promote-theirs archive-byte comparison fail on every UNTOUCHED archive (restore's failing scans keep the file) while passing on rewritten ones. Seed ours with the MULCH banner and theirs with the ML banner; then promoting theirs cancels the deviation for both untouched and rewritten files.

description: The reference CLI's interactive prompts (compact's 'Proceed with compaction? (y/N):' via readline on process.stdin) HANG when stdin is a closed stream under std Command::output — Bun's readline never sees EOF there. Differential batteries MUST pipe stdin explicitly for every interactive case (a run_in_feeding helper writing the answer then dropping the pipe); otherwise the reference side blocks forever and nextest dies on the outer timeout with two SLOW tests and no failure output (sprint 40 compact battery: 888s SIGTERM run before the fix, 19.7s after).
resolution: Pipe stdin for interactive reference runs; never rely on the closed-stream EOF.
